rules: Name = the English Wikipedia article title for the dish when one exists, checked through the Wikipedia API. A redirect counts as the title it lands on.
If there is no Wikipedia title, use the spelling found most often in at least 2 independent English food sources or menus, with URLs.

If there is no established spelling, use a simple transliteration that follows the dish's own country (Egyptian ج = g, Gulf/Najdi ق = g). No diacritics. Apostrophes only when the established spelling has one.
Keep a translated descriptor only when the name alone would mean nothing (Chicken Kabsa). Drop redundant ones: Hummus, not Hummus with Tahini; Sayadieh, not Fish Sayadieh.
Title Case. Articles and particles stay lowercase inside a name (el, al, bil, bel, bi). No abbreviations like 'w'. No ' - ' subtitles. Keep names short.
One Arabic word gets one English spelling everywhere, unless an established title differs on purpose (see wordDecisions).

Pronunciation is given only for names that contain transliterated words. It covers the Arabic-origin words only, in display order, with the stressed syllable in capitals. It skips English words (Chicken, Oven, Soup, Moroccan, Saudi) and the English food word Tagine.

Respelling conventions: gh = غ, kh = خ, AH = long a, moo- for مُ. ق follows the dish's dialect (a glottal stop in Cairo, g in the Gulf). Before a sun letter the article is written assimilated (esh-SHAHM, bir-RAD-da).
Meaning = one plain line of at most 10 words, built only from the recipe's own ingredients and steps, with no closing full stop. The same line is given in simple Modern Standard Arabic.

Same English name in more than one country: each one gets its country word before the name (Egyptian Sayadieh, Saudi Sayadieh), shown in the app as a coloured country tag, not as plain text. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-20.

wordDecisions.why: The Wikipedia title is 'Fatteh' and lists fatta and fattah as other romanizations, so every dish uses Fatteh: Fatteh, Chicken Fatteh, Lamb Fatteh and Eggplant Fatteh. 'Fattet' stays only in the construct form 'Fattet Hummus' (فتة حمص), the name Nigella and Food52 use. Pronunciation follows the country: Egyptian FAT-ta, Levantine FAT-teh. DECIDED 2026-11-21: the plain Egyptian dish (eg-fatta) uses 'Fattah', the spelling of Amira's Pantry, Daily News Egypt, Middle East Eye, Munaty Cooking and The Happy Foodie. Compound names keep Fatteh.

The Wikipedia title is 'Kofta', and 'Kafta' and 'Kefta' redirect to it. Egyptian and Levantine dishes use it (Grilled Kofta, Shrimp Kofta, Kofta with Tahini and Yogurt), said KOF-ta. Moroccan dishes use the Moroccan English spelling 'Kefta', as in Taste of Maroc, Salima's Kitchen and Splendid Table: Kefta Mkaouara, Moroccan Kefta Skewers and Gharb-Style Kefta, said KEF-ta. 'Kafta' remains the owner's option for the Levantine entry. DECIDED 2026-11-21: the Levantine grilled dish uses 'Kafta' (Saveur, SBS Food, The Matbakh, Maureen Abood), said KAF-ta, so Grilled Kofta became Grilled Kafta. Egyptian dishes keep Kofta.

The Wikipedia title is 'Tagine' ('Tajine' redirects), so every name uses it: Chicken Tagine with Green Olives, Fish Tagine with Chermoula, Meat Tagine with Cauliflower, Tilapia Tagine, Chicken Liver Tagine and Kaware Tagine. The exception is 'Tunisian Tajine', a different dish (a baked egg dish) whose established English name uses Tajine. Tagine counts as an English food word, so it has no pronunciation.

The Wikipedia title is 'Sayadieh'. The word already means a fish-and-rice dish, so 'Fish' is dropped from both the Egyptian and the Saudi entries. Pronunciation follows the country: Egyptian sai-ya-DAY-ya, Saudi sai-ya-DEE-ya.
'Maamoul' redirects to the Wikipedia title "Ma'amoul", so all three names keep the apostrophe. One respelling: ma-MOOL.
The Wikipedia title is 'Ful medames'. It is used in Ful Medames, Quick Ful Medames and Saudi Ful Medames, with one respelling: FOOL meh-DAM-mes.
'Shakshuka' redirects to the Wikipedia title 'Shakshouka'. One respelling: shak-SHOO-ka.
'Bessara' redirects to the Wikipedia title 'Bissara'. It is used for both the Egyptian and the Moroccan dish, with one respelling: bi-SAH-ra.
Based on common usage, because Wikipedia only redirects to Dolma. The same spelling appears in Mahshi, Hamam Mahshi, Malfouf Mahshi and Sheikh al-Mahshi.
The Wikipedia title is 'Hamam mahshi'. Hamam Mahshi and Hamam el Kazzab share the same spelling and the same respelling (ha-MAHM).
The English spelling used most (Petitchef, Egyptian Streets, Al-Ahram). Both entries share one Cairo respelling: ro-AH.
The Wikipedia titles are 'Kabsa' and 'Mandi (food)', with the bracket dropped. مجبوس stays 'Machboos', the Gulf spelling used by Gulf News and Foreign Fork, even though it redirects to Kabsa.

Each name follows its dish's established usage: the Egyptian 'Kabab Halla' (Chez Nermine, Cup of Yum, and the Serious Eats recipe cited by Wikipedia) and the Moroccan 'Kebab Maghdour' (Taste of Maroc). The plain English plural is 'Kebabs'.

Each country keeps its own convention. Maghreb dishes use 'Loubia' (Loubia with Meat, Loubia bel Kamoun), said LOOB-ya. The Lebanese dish uses 'Loubieh' (Loubieh bi Zeit). The Egyptian فاصوليا is 'Fasoulia', the Wikipedia title, because 'Fasolia' redirects to a Greek dish.
The Wikipedia title is 'Freekeh', used in Vegetable Freekeh and Chicken Freekeh Soup and said FREE-keh. The Algerian soup keeps its own Wikipedia title, 'Chorba frik'.
'Chorba' appears only inside the established Maghreb names (Chorba Frik, Chorba Fassia). Everywhere else the dish is named in plain English with 'Soup'.
'Kebda' appears inside the established Egyptian names (Kebda Eskandarani, Kebda bel Radda). The plain-English names use 'Liver' (Chicken Liver Tagine, Hejazi Liver, Saudi Liver Sandwich).

'Kousa' appears only in the established name 'Kousa bil Laban'. Everywhere else the name uses 'Zucchini', because the sources name those dishes in English (Zucchini with Eggs, Zucchini Bechamel Casserole).
The Wikipedia title is 'Musakhan'. One respelling with the doubled kh: moo-SAKH-khan.
The Wikipedia title is 'Maraq (dish)', with the bracket dropped. The respelling is MA-rag because Yemeni speech says ق as g.
Hejazi follows the Wikipedia title 'Hejazi Arabic'. Both words stay transliterated and get a respelling, unlike 'Saudi', which is an English word.

The article stays lowercase inside names: Halawet el Jibn, Hamam el Kazzab, Balah el Sham. 'al' is used only where the Wikipedia title has it (Sheikh al-Mahshi). Sun-letter assimilation appears only in the respelling (esh-SHAHM).

Levantine names use bi/bil (Loubieh bi Zeit, Riz bi Lahme, Samak bi Tahini, Kousa bil Laban). Egyptian and Maghreb names use bel (Kebda bel Radda, Loubia bel Kamoun). 'Macarona bil-Bechamel' keeps its Wikipedia form, hyphen included.
Every respelling writes غ as gh: gha-NOOSH, mogh-RAH-bee-yeh, mad-GHOOT, bagh-REER, magh-DOOR, GHARB.

entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API shows that 'Maamoul' redirects to "Ma'amoul", so the apostrophe is part of the established spelling. The ingredients are flour, semolina, butter and date paste. CONSISTENCY PASS: pronunciation: 'mah-MOOL' -> 'ma-MOOL' (one respelling for Ma'amoul).
consistencyEdits: pronunciation: 'mah-MOOL' -> 'ma-MOOL' (one respelling for Ma'amoul)

entries.meaningEn: Hulled wheat cooked with chicken or lamb and ghee
entries.meaningAr: قمح مقشور مطبوخ مع الدجاج أو اللحم والسمن
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia title 'Harees' exists. The ingredients are hulled wheat, chicken or lamb, and half a cup of ghee.

entries.meaningEn: Lamb and okra cooked in tomato with dried lime
entries.meaningAr: لحم غنم وبامية مطبوخان بالطماطم واللومي
entries.notes: verified. I confirmed that 'Bamia' redirects to 'Okra stew'. The article says these dishes are generally called 'okra stew' and in some cuisines just 'bamia'. The meaning matches the ingredients: lamb, okra, tomato and loomi.

entries.meaningEn: Flatbread soaked in lamb and vegetable stew
entries.meaningAr: خبز مغموس في مرق لحم الغنم والخضار
entries.notes: Name is verified. 'Thareed' redirects to 'Tharid', and that article describes this bread soup from Mecca. I CHANGED THE MEANING because the chickpeas are optional in the recipe. The required ingredients are lamb, tamees or Arabic bread, tomato, zucchini and carrot.

entries.meaningEn: Baked egg dish with chicken, potato, cheese and parsley
entries.meaningAr: طبق بيض مخبوز بالدجاج والبطاطس والجبن والبقدونس
entries.notes: Name is verified. I fetched MarocMama: its title is 'Tunisian Tajine', described as a spiced, frittata-like dish of chicken, potato, egg, cheese and parsley, baked until set. 'Tajine' redirects to 'Tagine', the Moroccan stew, which is a different dish. I CHANGED THE MEANING to add 'Baked', because step 8 of the recipe bakes it for 30–35 minutes. I dropped the Czech site as a weak source.

entries.meaningEn: Dough topped with spiced minced meat, tomato and pine nuts
entries.meaningAr: عجين مغطى باللحم المفروم المتبل والطماطم والصنوبر
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia title 'Sfiha' exists and describes a Levantine flatbread topped with minced meat, onion, tomato and pine nuts. The recipe has minced meat, tomato and pine nuts (صنوبر), plus pomegranate molasses, tahini and spices.

entries.meaningEn: Cardamom butter-and-ghee cookies stuffed with dates
entries.meaningAr: كعك بالهيل والزبدة والسمن محشو بالتمر
entries.notes: Name is verified. I CHANGED THE MEANING. The ingredient list has no dates, but steps 6–7 of the same recipe say to prepare dates and stuff each ball with them ('احشيه بالتمر'). The filling is in the recipe itself, so the meaning now names it. This also corrects the earlier note claiming the recipe has no filling. Data note: the dates appear only in the steps, so the ingredient list may be missing that line. CONSISTENCY PASS: pronunciation: 'mah-MOOL' -> 'ma-MOOL' (one respelling for Ma'amoul).
consistencyEdits: pronunciation: 'mah-MOOL' -> 'ma-MOOL' (one respelling for Ma'amoul)

entries.meaningEn: Oxtail soup with vegetables, dried lemon and hawaij spices
entries.meaningAr: شوربة ذيل بقري بالخضار والليمون المجفف وبهارات الحوائج
entries.notes: I CHANGED THE NAME from 'Marag' to 'Maraq'. The proposal missed that Wikipedia has 'Maraq (dish)' (fetched and confirmed), which describes a broth or soup of the Arabian Peninsula and is filed under Yemeni cuisine. As with 'Mandi (food)', the bracketed part is dropped. The Yemeni blog Yemeniyah also writes 'Maraq'. The 'Marag' page the proposal cited is only a disambiguation page. The pronunciation stays MA-rag, because Yemeni (Sanaani) speech says ق as g; the Yemen Cafe review writes 'marag'. I removed the toast.app source, which returned an error (403) and could not be checked. In the meaning I changed 'dried lime' to 'dried lemon', because the recipe line says '2 dried lemons'.

entries.meaningEn: Chicken simmered with potatoes, ginger, dried lime and hawaij
entries.meaningAr: دجاج مطهو مع البطاطس والزنجبيل والليمون المجفف والحوائج
entries.notes: I CHANGED THE NAME from 'Marag' to 'Maraq', for the same reason as the oxtail entry: the Wikipedia title is 'Maraq (dish)'. I searched and found no restaurant menu listing a 'chicken marag', and the menu sources the proposal cited cover lamb marag only, so I removed them. 'Chicken' is kept as the descriptor. I reworded the meaning so it describes the bone-in chicken simmered in water. The ingredients include '1 dried lemon or lime', ginger, potatoes and hawaij.

entries.meaningEn: Baked potatoes, peppers and celery in a garlic-herb lemon sauce
entries.meaningAr: بطاطس وفلفل رومي وكرفس مخبوزة بصلصة أعشاب بالثوم والليمون
entries.notes: Name is verified. I made a small change to the meaning to add 'baked', because the steps bake it for 55–65 minutes. The ingredients are red potatoes, three bell peppers, celery, cilantro, parsley, garlic and lemon.

entries.meaningEn: Chicken pieces marinated in lemon, garlic and fresh herbs
entries.meaningAr: قطع دجاج متبلة بالليمون والثوم والأعشاب الطازجة
entries.notes: verified. The ingredients are chicken breast, lemon zest and juice, garlic, parsley, rosemary and thyme. Adding 'Chicken' matches the Arabic name.

entries.meaningEn: Chicken, lamb and vegetable stew with chickpeas, over couscous
entries.meaningAr: مرق دجاج ولحم ضأن بالخضار والحمص يُقدَّم مع الكسكس
entries.notes: Name is verified. I CHANGED THE MEANING. Couscous is missing from the ingredient list, but the recipe step describes cooking pre-cooked couscous in chicken broth. The grain is therefore in the recipe and the meaning can name it. I dropped raisins to stay within 10 words. Data note: the ingredient list is missing the couscous line.

entries.meaningEn: Couscous topped with spiced sweet potato, broccoli, pepper and mint
entries.meaningAr: كسكس تعلوه بطاطا حلوة وبروكلي وفلفل متبلة مع النعناع
entries.notes: Name is verified. I CHANGED THE MEANING. The spices (cumin, cinnamon, chili flakes, saffron) go into the vegetables, not the couscous. The couscous is only toasted in oil and soaked in water. The recipe has a single red bell pepper, so 'peppers' became 'pepper'.

entries.meaningEn: Fried tilapia fillets with smoked paprika, cumin and ginger
entries.meaningAr: شرائح بلطي مقلية بالبابريكا المدخنة والكمون والزنجبيل
entries.notes: verified. The ingredients are tilapia fillets, frying oil, smoked paprika, cumin, ground coriander and ginger.

entries.meaningEn: Fava beans with olive oil, garlic, lemon and onion
entries.meaningAr: فول بزيت الزيتون والثوم والليمون والبصل
entries.notes: Name is verified: the Wikipedia title 'Ful medames' exists. I CHANGED THE PRONUNCIATION from 'FOOL meh-DAH-mes' to 'FOOL meh-DAM-mes'. Wikipedia gives [ˈfuːl meˈdæmmes], with a doubled m (مدمّس) and the stress on DAM, and Lebanese speech also stresses DAM. The meaning is verified against the ingredients: canned fava beans, olive oil, garlic, lemon juice and onion.

entries.meaningEn: Red lentil soup with potato, zucchini, chard and lemon
entries.meaningAr: شوربة عدس أحمر بالبطاطس والكوسة والسلق والليمون
entries.notes: verified. The ingredients are red lentils, Yukon gold potatoes, zucchini, Swiss chard and lemon juice.

entries.meaningEn: Brown rice and vegetable soup spiced with ras el hanout
entries.meaningAr: حساء أرز بني وخضار متبل برأس الحانوت
entries.notes: verified. The recipe file confirms brown rice, leek, eggplant, zucchini, carrot, vegetable broth and ras el hanout.

entries.meaningAr: أسياخ لحم بقري مفروم متبل بالبصل والثوم والبقدونس

entries.en: Egyptian Lentils with Rice and Pasta
entries.meaningEn: Lentils, rice and pasta with tomato-pepper sauce and fried onion
entries.meaningAr: عدس وأرز ومعكرونة بصلصة الطماطم والفلفل وبصل محمر
entries.notes: verified. Steps 4 and 5 confirm the pepper-tomato sauce and the fried onion garnish. The flag stands: in substance this is koshary (Wikipedia 'Koshary', which 'Kushari' redirects to), but the Arabic name is not كشري, so the literal name is kept.

entries.meaningEn: Butter cookies dipped in honey syrup and topped with walnuts
entries.meaningAr: كعك بالزبدة مغموس في شراب العسل ومزين بالجوز
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia title 'Ma'amoul' is confirmed and defines it as 'a filled cookie made with semolina flour and butter'. The flag stands: this recipe has no semolina and no filling (oil, butter, orange juice and flour, dipped in honey syrup and topped with walnuts). The Arabic name معمول needs owner review. If it changes, 'Lebanese Honey Walnut Cookies' is the plain-English fallback.

entries.meaningEn: Lamb and okra stewed in tomato sauce with spices
entries.meaningAr: لحم ضأن وبامية مطهوان في صلصة الطماطم بالبهارات
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API confirms that 'Bamia' and 'Bamya' redirect to 'Okra stew'. The article itself gives البامية باللحم as 'okra with meat' and mentions meatless variants, so 'with Meat' is justified. The recipe uses lamb and allows beef or goat.

entries.meaningEn: Blended red lentil soup with carrot, tomato, cumin and lemon
entries.meaningAr: شوربة عدس مضروبة بالخلاط مع الجزر والطماطم والكمون والليمون
entries.notes: Name verified. Changed the meaning: the toasted bread is optional in the recipe and should not define the dish. Lemon juice (a core ingredient) and blending (step 6) were added. The Arabic meaning now says just عدس, so it no longer clashes between أصفر and 'red'.

entries.meaningEn: Green beans and meat stewed in tomato sauce with carrots
entries.meaningAr: فاصوليا خضراء ولحم مطهوان في صلصة الطماطم مع الجزر
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API confirms that 'Fasoulia' is the green bean and tomato stew and that 'Fasolia' redirects to 'Fasolada', a different dish. The recipe file confirms green beans, meat, tomato, tomato paste and carrots.

entries.meaningEn: Cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley salad with lemon dressing
entries.meaningAr: سلطة خيار وطماطم وبصل وبقدونس بالليمون وزيت الزيتون
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API confirms the article 'Salata baladi' exists, and the ingredients match the recipe.

entries.meaningEn: Scrambled eggs with crisp basturma, cooked in ghee or butter
entries.meaningAr: بيض مخفوق مطهو مع البسطرمة المحمرة في السمن أو الزبدة
entries.notes: Name verified. I fetched amwhatieat, which uses 'Basturma' and the header 'Beid bel basturma - Eggs with basturma'. The Wikipedia API confirms 'Basturma' redirects to 'Pastirma'. Changed the meaning: the recipe whisks the eggs and scrambles them over crisped basturma (steps 1 to 3), so 'scrambled' and 'crisp' are more accurate than 'eggs cooked'.

entries.meaningEn: Beef liver sautéed with peppers, garlic, cumin and lemon
entries.meaningAr: كبدة بقري مشوحة مع الفلفل والثوم والكمون والليمون
entries.notes: Name verified, sources changed. The food.com URL is dead: it now 301-redirects to the fatafeat.com homepage, so I removed it. I fetched theodehlicious ('Kebda Eskandarani (Egyptian Liver Recipe)') and foodmap.in ('Kebda Eskandarani'), and both confirm the spelling. I added omaliegyptianfood (from search results) as a third source. Chez Nermine uses the variant 'Kebdah Eskandarani'.

entries.meaningEn: Baked eggplant layered with spiced ground beef and tomatoes
entries.meaningAr: باذنجان في الفرن في طبقات مع لحم بقري مفروم متبل وطماطم
entries.notes: Name verified. The Wikipedia 'Moussaka' article has a section on the Egyptian version, which supports keeping 'Egyptian'. The meaning now says 'baked' and 'layered', because the recipe bakes the eggplant and layers it with the meat sauce (steps 4, 8 and 9).

entries.meaningEn: Hard-boiled eggs fried in ghee or butter
entries.meaningAr: بيض مسلوق مقلي في السمن أو الزبدة
entries.notes: Name verified. I fetched Chez Nermine, which uses 'Beid Meza'lil' with an apostrophe and writes the Arabic بيض مزعلل. The Mediterranean Dish and Cup of Yum titles read 'Bied Meza'lil', so the apostrophe is part of the established spelling and 'Beid' is the more standard first word. Correction to the earlier flag: مزغلل is not necessarily a typo. The Mediterranean Dish suggests saying it 'meza-gh-lil', and homeisakitchen.com spells it 'mezaghlil', so both Arabic spellings are attested.

entries.meaningEn: Fava bean dip with dill, parsley and cilantro
entries.meaningAr: غموس فول مدشوش بالشبت والبقدونس والكزبرة الخضراء
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API confirms that 'Bessara' redirects to 'Bissara'. The recipe file confirms split fava beans with dill, parsley and cilantro.

entries.meaningEn: Layered phyllo pie filled with spiced ground beef
entries.meaningAr: فطيرة رقائق جلاش محشوة بلحم بقري مفروم متبل
entries.notes: verified. The source URL slugs all read 'egyptian-goulash', but feelgoodfoodie returned 403 when I fetched it. Wikipedia has no article for this dish. The recipe file confirms phyllo layers and a spiced ground beef filling.

entries.meaningEn: Fried patties of minced shrimp, herbs and chickpea flour
entries.meaningAr: أقراص مقلية من الجمبري المفروم والأعشاب ودقيق الحمص
entries.notes: verified. I fetched The Egyptian Epicurean, titled 'Shrimp kofta'. The recipe file confirms shrimp, parsley, dill, chickpea flour and egg, and the patties are fried.

entries.meaningEn: Potatoes and carrots baked with spiced ground meat and tomatoes
entries.meaningAr: بطاطس وجزر في الفرن مع لحم مفروم متبل وطماطم
entries.notes: verified. The recipe file allows ground beef or turkey, so 'Ground Meat' is correct, and it confirms the potatoes, carrots and tomatoes.

entries.meaningAr: بسلة وجزر مطهوان في صلصة طماطم متبلة
entries.notes: verified. The recipe file confirms peas, carrots, tomato sauce, coriander and paprika.

entries.meaningAr: كعك هش بالسمن والسكر البودرة مع شرائح اللوز
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API confirms that 'Ghoriba' and 'Ghraybeh' redirect to 'Ghorayeba'. The almonds are optional in the recipe but are the usual topping.

entries.meaningAr: شعيرية حلوة بالزبدة تعلوها عجة بيض بالزعفران

entries.meaningAr: أرز بسمتي متبل مطهو مع الدجاج واللومي
entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia API confirms that 'Majboos' and 'Machboos' redirect to 'Kabsa', and the article reads 'also known as ... Machboos (Gulf Arabic: مچبوس [mətʃˈbuːs])', which supports the 'ch' pronunciation. I fetched Foreign Fork, titled 'Chicken Machboos Recipe'.

entries.notes: Name verified (the Wikipedia API confirms the article). Changed the meaning: the shrak bread is optional in the recipe, so it should not define the dish. It now names the turmeric rice and toasted almonds, which are core ingredients in the recipe file.

entries.meaningEn: Beef meatballs and potatoes in tomato sauce with pine nuts
entries.meaningAr: كرات لحم بقري وبطاطس في صلصة طماطم مع الصنوبر
entries.notes: CHANGED from 'Dawood Basha' to 'Daoud Basha'. There is no Wikipedia article (a Wikipedia search returns nothing). The proposal's lead source (tasteofbeirut.com/lebanese-meatballs-dawood-basha) returns 404, so it was dropped. A web search shows the two spellings about evenly used: Daoud on butfirstchai, Cup of Yum (fetched and confirmed), Rove Hotels, Philips, CDKitchen and Lebanon's Taste & Flavors; Dawood on Munaty, Maggi Arabia, Falasteeni Foodie and ExpatWoman. On a tie I kept the current spelling so the name does not change for no gain. The pronunciation was changed to match it: Lebanese داود is da-OOD. Meaning verified: pine nuts are the garnish and pomegranate molasses is optional.

entries.notes: verified. The Wikipedia article title is 'Batata harra' (fetched). The meaning matches the recipe: potatoes, coriander, lemon juice, chili paste and garlic.

spellingDecisions.evidence: Saudi/Hejazi sources write 'Mutabbaq': ButFirstChai, Theodehlicious, House of Saud Jeddah and Riyadh street-food guides, Expatica, D Magazine (2026). 'Murtabak' is the Southeast Asian name of the wider family.

'Luqaimat' is the spelling used by Gulf News, The National, Gulf Today, Khaleej Times, the Michelin Guide Dubai and Munaty Cooking. 'Lokma' is the Turkish family name; Saveur's 'Lgeimat' is a one-off.

Every English source on the Egyptian dish uses 'Balah el Sham': Egyptian Epicurean, Amira's Pantry, Arla Foods UK, Gulf Times, Afrifoodnetwork, Onmanorama. 'Tulumba' is the Turkish/Balkan name and is not used for the Egyptian sweet.

Levantine sources write 'Kafta' for this grilled skewer: Saveur 'Kafta (Lebanese Beef Kebabs)', SBS Food 'Kafta skewers', The Matbakh 'Lebanese Grilled Kafta Skewers', Maureen Abood 'Lebanese Beef Kafta'. Same per-country rule as Moroccan 'Kefta'; Egyptian dishes keep 'Kofta'.

English sources on the Egyptian Eid dish write 'Fattah': Amira's Pantry, Daily News Egypt, Middle East Eye, Munaty Cooking, The Happy Foodie (Munira Mahmud), Petitchef. 'Fatteh' is the Levantine form; Chez Nermine's 'Fatta' is a minority spelling.

Lebanese restaurant menus list it as 'Warak Enab' (ilili NYC/DC, Al Wadi), and recipe sites title it 'Warak Enab' (The Matbakh, Hungry Paprikas, Theodehlicious). Owner rule prefers the established dish name over a plain-English description.

'Msemmen/Msemen' is far more used in English than 'Rghaif' (Wikipedia title Msemmen, Taste of Maroc, Tasting Table, Morocco World News, Salima's Kitchen); Rghaif appears mostly as an aside. Kept the Wikipedia double-m spelling; 'Msemen' is the common single-m variant.
